chapters.title: Replies, notes and templates
intro: This chapter is for agents and supervisors who write to customers and colleagues from a ticket.

It explains the composer: replies, internal notes, handover notes, templates, attachments and drafts. It also covers the side tabs and composer buttons that other modules add, such as **Blueprint** and **Draft with AI**.

sections.title: The composer
intro: The composer sits at the bottom of every ticket. When it is closed, it shows three buttons: **Reply**, **Internal note** and **Handover**.
Select a button, or press [[R]] for a reply or [[N]] for a note. The composer opens with the editor ready for typing.

blocks.caption: The closed composer with its three buttons.
blocks.alt: Composer bar with Reply, Internal note and Handover buttons

blocks.caption: The open composer on an e-mail ticket, with a reply typed in.
blocks.alt: Open composer with numbered highlights on the message type, recipients, editor, attach button, Templates, Draft with AI and Send

callouts: The message type: **Reply**, **Internal note** or **Handover**. Below it are the draft status and the **Minimise** button.
Recipients. **To** holds the contact's e-mail address. The **Cc** and **Bcc** links add more rows.
The editor with its formatting toolbar.
**Draft with AI**: writes a draft reply for you to check.
**Send**, and the arrow next to it for **Send and set status**.

blocks.note: Some roles may only view a ticket. For them, the bar shows **You can view this ticket but not reply to it.** Light agents can add internal notes but cannot reply to customers.

sections.title: Reply to a customer
sections.intro: Send an answer to the customer on the ticket's channel.
steps: Select **Reply**, or press [[R]].
For an e-mail ticket, check the address in **To**. Select **Cc** or **Bcc** to add more people.
Write your reply in the editor. To start from a template, open **Templates** and choose one.
To add files, select **Attach files** and choose them.
Select **Send**, or press [[Ctrl+Enter]].
sections.result: The message **Reply sent** appears, and the reply appears at the end of the conversation. An open or assigned ticket moves to **In Progress**.

list: On e-mail tickets, **Send** works only when **To** has at least one address.
Type an address in **To**, **Cc** or **Bcc** and press [[Enter]]. Select **×** on an address to remove it.
**Bcc** recipients are hidden from the others. Saved drafts do not keep them.
On other channels, the composer shows **Sent to** with the contact's name and channel, such as WhatsApp. The reply goes out on that channel.

blocks.tip: Your e-mail signature from **My profile** is added to e-mail replies. It does not show in the composer.

sections.title: Send a reply and change the status
sections.intro: Send your reply and set the next status in one step. For example, send a question and set **Waiting on Customer**.
prerequisites: The reply has text and, on e-mail tickets, a recipient.
steps: Write your reply.

steps.caption: The **Send and set status** menu.
steps.alt: Send and set status menu listing Open, In Progress, Waiting on Customer, Waiting on Third Party, Escalated to Engineering and Resolved

steps: Choose the status.
sections.result: The reply is sent, and the ticket gets the new status. The message **Reply sent and status updated** appears.

blocks.note: The menu only lists statuses allowed next. Closed statuses are never in the list.

sections.title: Add an internal note
sections.intro: Write a note that only agents see, such as what you tried or a question for a colleague.
prerequisites: You need the add notes permission.
steps: Select **Internal note**, or press [[N]].
Write the note.

steps.text: To bring in a colleague, type `@` and the first letters of their name. Choose the person in the list.
steps.caption: An internal note with the mention list open after typing `@Mee`.
steps.alt: Internal note composer with an amber background and a mention list showing Meera Iyer

steps: Select **Add note**.
sections.result: The message **Note added** appears. The note shows in the conversation with an amber background and an **Internal note** label.

blocks.note: Everyone you mention gets a notification. Mentioned colleagues also become collaborators on the ticket.

blocks.warning: Never paste information meant for the customer into a note. Customers do not see notes, so the customer never gets it.

sections.title: Write a handover note
sections.intro: Leave a note for the next agent, for example at the end of your shift.
prerequisites: You need the add notes permission.
steps: Select **Handover**.

steps.text: Answer the question in the editor: **What should the next agent know?**
steps.caption: A handover note before it is added.
steps.alt: Handover composer with a note for the next agent and an Add handover button

steps: Select **Add handover**.
sections.result: The message **Handover note added** appears. The note shows in the conversation with an amber background. Only agents see it.

blocks.note: Internal notes and handover notes share one draft. Text you type in one also shows in the other until you add it or discard it.

sections.title: Use a reply template
sections.intro: Templates give you ready-made answers to common questions. SupportDesk fills in names and numbers for you.
steps: Open the composer in **Reply** mode.
Place the cursor where the template text should go.

steps.caption: The **Templates** menu, grouped by category.
steps.alt: Templates menu with an Engineering group containing Fix released and a Follow-up group containing Waiting on customer gentle reminder

steps: Read the inserted text and change it to fit the ticket.
Send the reply.
sections.result: The template text appears in the editor with the customer's and the ticket's details filled in.

rows: The contact's first name, or **there** when there is no contact.

list: A template can be personal, or shared with a team, a department or the whole workspace.
If no template is available to you, the menu shows **No templates available**.

blocks.note: You cannot create or change templates in the desk. Ask your administrator for new templates. Templates insert text only. They do not change the ticket.

sections.title: Attach files
sections.intro: Add screenshots, logs or documents to a reply or a note.
steps: In the open composer, select **Attach files** (the paperclip).
Choose one or more files, then confirm.
Wait until each file's progress bar disappears.
To remove a file, select **×** next to its name.
sections.result: The files are listed under the editor. They go out with the reply or note.

list: The size limit depends on your plan. The standard limit is 25 MB per file.
Programs and active content are blocked, such as `.exe`, `.js`, `.html`, `.svg` and `.docm` files.
Every file is scanned for malware. A file that fails shows **Blocked by the virus scanner**.
**Send** waits until every file has uploaded.

sections.title: Drafts
intro: The composer saves your text as a draft about a second after you stop typing. The draft status above the editor shows **Saving draft…**, then **Draft saved** and the time.
Drafts come back when you reopen the ticket, on any device. When the composer is closed, a **Draft saved** badge shows that a draft is waiting.

list: Select **Minimise** (the down arrow) to close the composer and keep the draft.
Select **Discard** to delete the draft and close the composer. You cannot undo this.
Replies and notes have separate drafts. Internal notes and handover notes share one draft.

blocks.note: If the status shows **Draft not saved**, keep the composer open and check your connection. Your text stays in the editor.

sections.title: When someone posts while you write
intro: A customer or a colleague may post on the ticket while you write your reply. Then SupportDesk does not send your reply straight away.
A yellow panel opens above the editor. It says how many entries were added while you were writing and shows each of them.

steps: Read the new entries in the panel.
To change your reply first, select **I've reviewed them — keep editing**.
To send your reply as it is, select **Send anyway**.

blocks.tip: Always read the new entries. The customer may have answered your question already.

sections.title: Draft a reply with AI
sections.intro: Let the AI assistant write a first draft from the ticket and your knowledge base. You check and send it.
prerequisites: You need the AI permission, and your plan must include AI.
steps: Open the composer in **Reply** mode.
Select **Draft with AI**.
Read the message under the editor. It says how many sources the draft used.
Check and edit the draft.
Select **Send**.
sections.result: The draft appears in the editor. If the editor already had text, the draft is added at the cursor.

blocks.warning: If no matching article or resolved ticket was found, the message says so. Check such a draft with extra care before you send it.

sections.title: Share a ticket to Teams or Slack
sections.intro: Post a ticket to a Microsoft Teams or Slack channel to ask colleagues for help.
prerequisites: You need the add notes permission.
An administrator has added the channel under **Administration** > **Teams & Slack**.
steps: Select **Internal note**.
Type a comment in the editor if you like. SupportDesk adds it to the post.

steps.caption: The **Share to Teams / Slack** dialog in a workspace without channels.
steps.alt: Share to Teams or Slack dialog showing No channels and a hint for administrators

steps: In **Channel**, choose the channel.
In **Message**, enter a short text for the top of the post.
Select **Share**.
sections.result: The message **Shared to** and the channel name appears under the editor. The post links back to the ticket.

sections.title: Side tabs from other modules
sections.intro: Other modules add tabs to the **Ticket details** panel. You only see a tab when you have its permission and your plan includes it.

rows: Shows the guided process the ticket follows and the next steps you may run. See [Follow a blueprint](#rn-blueprint).
You may use AI, and your plan includes it.

Summary, sentiment, expected resolution and classification. It also offers a suggested reply with **Insert into composer**, similar and duplicate tickets, the likely root cause, **Draft article** and **Run agents**.
You may link or view engineering work items.
Lists linked engineering work items with their state, fix version and release. **Escalate to engineering** creates a work item. **Link existing** links one that already exists.

blocks.p: The composer also gets extra buttons from other modules. **Draft with AI** appears in **Reply** mode. **Share to Teams/Slack** appears in **Internal note** mode.

sections.title: Follow a blueprint
sections.intro: A blueprint guides a ticket through set steps, such as investigation, review and release. You move the ticket to its next step on the **Blueprint** tab.
prerequisites: The ticket follows a blueprint. Otherwise the tab says **This ticket doesn't follow a blueprint**.
steps: Select **Ticket details**, then the **Blueprint** tab.
Check the steps of the process and the **Current state**.

steps.text: Select the transition you want to run, such as **Confirm defect**.
steps.caption: The **Blueprint** tab with the **Confirm defect** transition open. It needs approval and two fields.
steps.alt: Blueprint tab with the process states, the current state Investigation, and an open transition form with Severity, Version and Comment

steps: Fill in the required fields that appear.
Enter a **Comment**. The step may make it mandatory.
Select **Move to** and the state name, or **Request approval** when the step needs approval.
sections.result: The ticket moves to the next state, and its status changes with it. For an approval step, the tab shows that the step is waiting for approval.

list: An **approval** badge means a supervisor must approve the step. The request appears on the **Approvals** page.
A badge such as **2 fields** shows how many required fields are still empty.
Some steps are greyed out, with the reason below them.
If no step is open to you, the tab says **No transitions are available to you from this state.**

blocks.note: People who manage automation also see **Remove ticket from blueprint**. Removing it lets the ticket change status freely again.

sections.title: Composer buttons
sections.intro: Every button and field you can find in the open composer.

rows: Switch the message type. Notes and handovers have an amber background.
Closes the composer and keeps the draft.
E-mail recipients. Only shown on e-mail tickets.
Bold, italic, underline, strike-through, lists, quotes, links and code. Press [[Ctrl+K]] in the editor to add a link.
Inserts a reply template. **Reply** mode only.
Writes a draft reply. **Reply** mode only, when AI is available.
Posts the ticket to a Teams or Slack channel. **Internal note** mode only.
Deletes the draft and closes the composer.
Sends the reply or adds the note. [[Ctrl+Enter]] does the same.

troubleshooting.cause: The editor is empty, a file is still uploading, or an e-mail reply has no address in **To**.
troubleshooting.fix: Write the message, wait for the uploads, and add a recipient.

troubleshooting.problem: The composer shows **You can view this ticket but not reply to it.**
troubleshooting.cause: Your role may view the ticket but not reply or add notes.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask your administrator for the reply or note permission, or ask a colleague to reply.

troubleshooting.problem: A panel says that new entries were added while you were writing.
troubleshooting.cause: The customer or a colleague posted on the ticket after you started typing.
troubleshooting.fix: Read the entries. Select **I've reviewed them — keep editing**, or **Send anyway**.

troubleshooting.problem: The reply was not sent, and a message says your text is kept.
troubleshooting.cause: The connection dropped, or SupportDesk refused the reply.
troubleshooting.fix: Check your connection and try again. Your text stays in the composer.

troubleshooting.problem: The draft status shows **Draft not saved**.
troubleshooting.cause: SupportDesk could not save the draft, often because of the connection.
troubleshooting.fix: Keep the composer open. The draft saves again when you type, once the connection is back.

troubleshooting.cause: No template is shared with you, and you have no personal templates.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask your administrator to add templates for your team or department.

troubleshooting.problem: An attachment shows **Blocked by the virus scanner**.
troubleshooting.cause: The malware scan found a problem in the file.
troubleshooting.fix: Remove the file and attach a clean copy.

troubleshooting.cause: No Teams or Slack channel is set up for the workspace.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask your administrator to add one under **Administration** > **Teams & Slack**.

faq.q: Do customers ever see internal notes or handover notes?
faq.a: No. Only agents see them. The customer portal never shows them, and replies never include them.

faq.q: I closed the browser while writing. Is my reply lost?
faq.a: No. The composer saves a draft as you type. Open the ticket again on any device to carry on.

faq.q: Can I create my own reply templates?
faq.a: Not in the desk. Ask your administrator to add the template for you.

faq.q: Why did my colleague become a collaborator?
faq.a: You mentioned them with `@` in an internal note. Mentioning someone adds them as a collaborator and notifies them.

glossary.definition: The writing area at the bottom of a ticket, used for replies, internal notes and handover notes.
A note on a ticket that only agents can see. It has an amber background.
An internal note for the next agent who works on the ticket.
Ready-made reply text with placeholders that SupportDesk fills in, such as the contact's name.
A code in a template, such as {{contact.name}}, that SupportDesk replaces with real details.
An unsent reply or note that SupportDesk saves as you type.
Typing @ and a colleague's name in a note. It notifies them and makes them a collaborator.
When someone posts on a ticket while you are writing a reply. SupportDesk shows the new entries before you send.
